name: Nuru Yuzu-Ginger Stim Rocks
manufacturer: Nuru Street Candy (unlicensed street brand, Tier 1-2)
description: Rough-cut popping candy rocks infused with a caffeine-adjacent plant alkaloid and yuzu-ginger oil. They pop and fizz on the tongue while delivering a fast-acting mild stimulant effect that peaks in about ten minutes.
flavor_profile: Sharp yuzu citrus burst, ginger heat that builds with each pop, clean stimulant warmth without jitteriness
cultural_context: Nuru rocks are Shelf staple stimulants, sold from jacket pockets and folding tables in transit corridors. They're not illegal but they're not licensed either, which means no quality assurance — the alkaloid concentration varies batch to batch. Users develop a tolerance quickly and most take them before physical labor or long walks through dangerous districts. There's no pretense of wellness branding.
story_hooks: A recent Nuru batch from an unknown supplier has a significantly higher alkaloid concentration than usual, and two workers have been hospitalized with cardiac events — but tracing an unlicensed street brand's supply chain is nearly impossible.
A Tier 3 food safety inspector develops a secret habit with Nuru rocks after a stressful reassignment to the Shelf, and is terrified her colleagues will find the sachets in her kit bag.

The person who formulates Nuru's popping candy compound is a former licensed pharmaceutical chemist who walked away from a corponation contract and now operates out of a converted shipping container — and someone from her past has just found her.
